title: Affine pro-etale subsite computes the small pro-etale topos
statement:
Let $X$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme] with its small pro-etale site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and compatible universes and skeletons [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $X_{\mathrm{aff,proet}}$ be the full subsite whose objects are affine weakly etale maps $U\to X$, with standard pro-etale coverings (finite families of affine weakly etale maps satisfying the covering condition of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]). Restriction along the inclusion induces an equivalence of topoi
$$\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{proet}})\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{aff,proet}}).$$

source.place: Tag 098W, label lemma-alternative: restriction from $S_{\mathrm{proetale}}$ to $S_{\mathrm{affine,proetale}$

proof.text: Write $\mathcal C=X_{\mathrm{aff,proet}}$, $\mathcal D=X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, and let $u$ be the full inclusion. An open immersion is étale and hence weakly étale by the two cited comparison statements. Composition stability therefore makes every affine open $A\subset U$ of a weakly étale $U\to X$ an object of $\mathcal C$. Affine opens cover $U$ by the affine-basis lemma. The family of all affine opens $A\to U$ is a pro-etale covering directly by the covering definition: for any affine open $W\subset U$, the member $A=W$ alone has image $W$. Thus every object of $\mathcal D$ has a covering by image objects. This works for arbitrary $U$ and $X$, with no quasi-compactness or separatedness assumption.

source.place: Tag 098W (lemma-alternative), image-object covering condition of Tag 03A0; affine opens: 01IT; open immersions: 02GP and 094X; composition: 094T

proof.text: For a finite family $\{A_j\to U\}$ of weakly étale maps with all $A_j$ and $U$ affine, the pro-etale covering condition is equivalent to $\bigcup_j\operatorname{im}(A_j\to U)=U$. Necessity follows by taking the affine open $U$ itself in the definition. For sufficiency, fix any affine open $W\subset U$. Each inverse image $A_j\times_U W$ is an affine open of $A_j$ by the cited affine-morphism theorem; these finitely many opens have images with union $W$. This is exactly the finite-affine-refinement condition in the definition. In particular the standard coverings used here agree with Tag 098E, not with an ind-etale presentation condition.

The declared standard coverings make $\mathcal C$ a site and $u$ continuous. Indeed, a pullback $A\times_U B$ needed for a covering in $\mathcal C$ is affine by the affine-spectra fibre-product theorem. Its map to $B$ is weakly étale by base-change stability, and its composite to $X$ is weakly étale by composition stability. Thus this is also the pullback in the full subcategory. Pro-etale coverings are precisely fpqc families of weakly étale arrows by the site definition. The three fpqc covering axioms, together with weakly étale base-change and composition stability, show that singleton isomorphisms, finite composites of standard coverings, and their pullbacks are standard coverings again: the index sets remain finite, and all their domains remain affine. The inclusion preserves these covering families and their pullbacks, which is exactly continuity in the cited site definition.

source.place: Tag 098W (lemma-alternative), continuity verification; Tags 098C (lemma-proetale), 01I4/01JQ (affine fibre products), 022D (fpqc covering axioms)

proof.text: To check cocontinuity, let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal C$ and $\{V_i\to U\}$ any covering of $\mathcal D$. Apply the defining covering condition to the affine open $U\subset U$: it gives finitely many affine opens $A_j\subset V_{i(j)}$ whose composite images cover $U$. Step 1 makes the open inclusions weakly étale, and composition stability makes $A_j\to U$ and $A_j\to X$ weakly étale. By step 2 the finite family $\{A_j\to U\}$ is a standard covering in $\mathcal C$. Each arrow factors through the chosen $V_{i(j)}$, so its image family refines the original covering. This is precisely the cocontinuity condition, with the required factors explicitly given by $A_j\hookrightarrow V_{i(j)}$.

Because $\mathcal C$ is a full subcategory, $u(a)=u(b)$ for parallel arrows implies $a=b$; the singleton identity covering witnesses local faithfulness. Every arrow $c:u(U^{\prime})\to u(U)$ is already the image of a unique arrow $U^{\prime}\to U$; again the singleton identity covering witnesses local fullness. Together with continuity in step 3, cocontinuity in step 4 and the image-object coverings in step 1, these verify all five conditions in the cited definition of a special cocontinuous functor.

Use the compatible universes and small skeletons of the stated pro-etale site convention, and apply the special-cocontinuous sheaf-equivalence theorem to $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$. Its hypotheses have all been verified in steps 1–5. Its inverse-image functor is precomposition with $u$, hence on objects it sends $F$ to $F|_{\mathcal C}$ and on morphisms it restricts each component to affine objects. Therefore restriction is the asserted equivalence $\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{proet}})\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{aff,proet}})$, and the cited theorem identifies it with an equivalence of topoi.

proof_origin.place: Tag 098W (lemma-alternative): expanded verification of the five hypotheses of Sites Tag 03A0, with finite affine refinement from 098D and standard coverings from 098E.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NH-d9501b3e9 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all six steps in full, together with every cited node's statement (11 nodes plus the fpqc, pro-étale covering, small pro-étale site and weakly étale definitions). The statement matches Stacks 098W (proetale.tex lemma-alternative, l.2696) with the coverings of 098E; Stacks writes S_affine,etale in its display, which is a typo for S_affine,proetale, and the item uses the correct site. Step 1 gives cover-density (03A0(5)): 02GP and etale-implies-weakly-etale plus composition put affine opens in the site, and the family of all affine opens is a covering because each affine open W is itself a member. Step 2 shows that standard coverings are exactly the pro-étale coverings of an affine target, using 01SH as that node states it (098D/098E). Step 3 shows the affine subcategory is a site and the inclusion is continuous: fibre products are taken over an affine U (01I4/01JQ), so no quasi-separatedness of X is used, and the site axioms come from 022D/098C plus weakly-étale stability. Step 4 gives cocontinuity through the finite affine refinement of the affine target, matching clause (1) of the special-cocontinuous definition. Step 5 is correctly marked elementary: local fullness and faithfulness hold for a full inclusion, witnessed by identity coverings. Step 6 applies the 03A0 node, whose statement says the inverse image is precomposition, i.e. restriction; this agrees with the 03A0 proof (g^{-1}G(U)=G(u(U))). Edge cases checked: empty X, the empty covering of an empty affine, non-quasi-compact and non-quasi-separated X, and infinite coverings. There are no new nodes. A search found no pro-étale duplicate; the étale analogue lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-site-topos is a different site, and the Lean AffineProEt is narrower. tools/review_split.py reports PASS.
